title: Polycarp of Smyrna
lead: Polycarp led the church at Smyrna in Asia (western Turkey) in the first half of the second century and was burned to death there, at eighty-six, most probably in AD 155. Irenaeus, who heard him as a boy, remembered him as a disciple of John and of others who had seen the Lord. His one surviving letter, to the Philippians, and the account of his death, the Martyrdom of Polycarp, are both on this site; no church counts either as Scripture.

sections.b: Irenaeus, writing while Eleutherius was bishop of Rome (Against Heresies 3.3.3), says Polycarp 'was not only instructed by apostles, and conversed with many who had seen Christ, but was also, by apostles in Asia, appointed bishop of the Church in Smyrna', that he visited Rome in the time of Anicetus, and that he called Marcion 'the first-born of Satan' (Against Heresies 3.3.4, ANF translation). In a letter to Florinus, Irenaeus recalled where Polycarp sat when he taught and how he told of 'his intercourse with John and with the others who had seen the Lord' (Eusebius, Church History 5.20.6). Eusebius adds that Polycarp's letter used 1 Peter (Church History 4.14.9), and Jerome that the letter was still 'read ... in the meetings in Asia' (Lives of Illustrious Men 17). Lake's introduction: 'opinions differ' whether his teacher was John the son of Zebedee or John the Elder.
sections.refs: Revelation 2:8-11; Polycarp to the Philippians 1:0; Martyrdom of Polycarp 9:3

sections.b: Polycarp is honored as a saint and martyr on 23 February. The Orthodox Church in America commemorates 'Hieromartyr Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna', a martyred bishop. The U.S. Catholic bishops' liturgical calendar lists 'Saint Polycarp, Bishop and Martyr' on that day. The Church of England's Common Worship calendar lists 'Polycarp, Bishop of Smyrna, Martyr, c.155' on that day. The Lutheran Church—Missouri Synod commemorates 'Polycarp of Smyrna, Pastor and Martyr', who it says was executed 'on February 23, c. 156', a year later than Lake's date.
